detail.longDescription: I'm building a real-time voice AI system and am specifically trying to reduce the delay between the end of a user's utterance and the start of the assistant's response. For a streaming STT → LLM → TTS pipeline, what architecture and component choices have you used to achieve a first audible response within approximately 500 ms? In particular, I'm interested in production measurements for: End-of-utterance detection Final STT result delivery LLM time to first token TTS time to first audio chunk Audio transport and playback buffering Please include the transport and orchestration approach you use, along with any optimizations that materially reduced this end-to-end latency. If you have benchmark data, please clarify how latency was measured and whether the 500 ms target was achieved consistently or only at a particular percentile.
